ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the picture is a rectangular prism, and the picture only shows the situation where two of its top corners have been obliquely cut off; these cuts have triangular cross-sections, indicating that each corner is cut off in the same way. Then reason: The problem states that all 8 corners of the rectangular prism are cut off. The original 6 rectangular faces each have 4 corners shaved off, so each rectangular face will change from a quadrilateral into an octagon, producing a total of 6×8=48 face-edge correspondences. Each cut-off corner will form a new triangular face, and 8 corners form 8 triangular faces, with a total of 8×3=24 face-edge correspondences. The total number of face-edge correspondences is 48+24=72. Each actual edge is counted jointly by two faces, so the number of edges of the new figure is 72÷2=36.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a rectangular prism with corner truncations: the shown cuts are triangular slices across corners, illustrating the same type of cut to be made at every corner. From the text, use that all 8 corners are cut off, even though only 2 are drawn. Count edges by counting faces after truncation: the original 6 rectangular faces of the prism each have their 4 corners clipped, so each becomes an octagon with 8 edges. Each of the 8 removed corners creates one new triangular face with 3 edges. The total face-edge incidences are 6×8 + 8×3 = 48 + 24 = 72. Since every edge is shared by exactly 2 faces, divide by 2 to get 36 edges.
